newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse grows, reverses slack activity.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse grows, reverses slack activity.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Thursday it had reversed a sluggish 1996 trend in the first half of this year, with several factors combining to move its main indicators higher.
Total volume in the first six months of this year soared to 206 million shares from 1.1 million in 1996 as a whole, with overall turnover rising almost 40 times to 577.5 billion lei.

Technical improvements to make activity more efficient, including cross deals and group account trading, higher liquidity, as well as the start of custodian services combined to lead the market higher, the statement said.
The bourse still lacks its own market index. But three independent indices hit several all-time highs this year, reflecting the bullish mood dominating the market.
"New foreign investment rules, political stability and a market boasting trading facilities and higher liquidity were strong incentives for big local and foreign investors," a broker said.
The bourse, which started with some 10 stocks late in 1995, now lists 46 companies, eight of which trade on the first tier.
Market capitalisation surged to 4.3 trillion lei at the end of June from a scant 235 billion at the start of the year, the statement showed.
Romania also operates an over-the-counter (OTC) market, which lists more than 3,000 companies. At end-June, OTC capitalisation was 14.7 trillion lei.
Dozens of companies, including high-caps and a local bank, are expected in bourse trading before the end of the year and another 2,000 companies also plan to join the OTC market.
"With liquidity promising to grow and big foreign investors in the market, we have every reason to believe in a sound future for Romanian equities," an analyst said.
Foreign investors came to the Romanian equity market only this year, drawn by the centrist government's promises of strong support for capital markets and foreign investment.

The centrists, who took office after ousting leftists in elections last November, have brought in fresh foreign investment rules, including portfolio inflows, vowing also to put a large number of state companies into the market for privatisation. ($=7,054 lei)
